chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the supererogatory prayers on Friday. He said: Six rakʿahs at the beginning of the day, six rakʿahs before zawāl, two rakʿahs when the sun passes the meridian, and six rakʿahs after الجمعة; that makes twenty rakʿahs besides the obligatory prayer. And what I practice upon and give fatwa by is that bringing forward all the nawāfil on Friday to before zawāl is more excellent; this indicates that.

key_terms.التَّطَوُّعِ: supererogatory prayer or voluntary devotional act
key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: the sun’s decline from the meridian, marking midday
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, the weekly congregational day

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred time for the Friday supererogatory prayers in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the arrangement of the supererogatory prayers on Friday and counts them as twenty rakʿahs in addition to the obligatory prayer. It also states that the preferred ruling is to perform all the Friday nawāfil before zawāl, indicating a juristic preference regarding their timing.
